title: How is work stress showing up for you?
intro: Work stress doesn't always stay at work. Sometimes it follows people home mentally, emotionally, and physically — especially in demanding environments where people are expected to keep functioning no matter how overwhelmed they feel. This check-in is designed to help you understand how workplace stress and burnout may currently be affecting you.

options.text: Mentally nonstop even outside of work hours
Exhausting but I keep pushing through
Overwhelming because others rely on me
Disconnected and hard to stay motivated in

questions.text: When work stress builds up, I usually:

options.text: Take stress home mentally and struggle turning work off
Absorb other people's emotions and tension
Ignore my own needs to keep everything running
My nervous system feels emotionally overloaded
I haven't fully rested in a long time
I'm carrying too much responsibility for others
I feel emotionally disconnected from work lately

questions.text: People around me probably see me as:
What do you need most right now?

a.description: You struggle disconnecting mentally from work and feel constantly "on." Even off the clock, work has a way of staying present in your mind.

b.description: You absorb stress, tension, and emotions from workplace environments. It can be hard to tell which feelings are yours and which belong to others.

c.description: You push through exhaustion to maintain productivity and expectations. Your output stays high — but it's coming at a real cost.

d.description: You feel pressure holding everything together for others while overwhelmed internally. Leading others doesn't leave much room to take care of yourself.

e.description: You feel emotionally disconnected from work, motivation, or purpose. Something that used to feel meaningful may feel distant right now.
